sections.learningObjectives:
- Follow manufacturer test-kit instructions and office policy exactly when supporting waived point-of-care testing, including specimen type, timing, storage, and expiration.
- Perform and document internal and external quality control, including running controls, recording results, and tracking lot numbers and storage conditions.
- Recognize invalid quality control and invalid test results and escalate to the appropriate supervisor or clinician per office policy without reporting invalid results as valid.
- Record test and quality-control results accurately, completely, and legibly at the time of testing, within the assistant's scope of practice.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

The package insert is like a recipe card that came with a baking kit. Even if you have seen a friend bake before, you read the card first so you do every step exactly right.

### Question 2

If you buy a new board game, the instructions inside the box are the exact rules for that game. The package insert is the instructions inside the test box.

### Question 3

If a friend shows you a shortcut that is different from the recipe, you check the recipe and ask an adult which one is right. The written rules win, and a supervisor can settle the disagreement.

### Question 4

Waived means the test is like a very easy recipe, but you still have to follow the recipe. Easy does not mean you can skip the steps.

### Question 5

Some things are like cookies: if you check them before the timer goes off or long after, they are not done right. The test has a timer window, and you look only during that window.

### Question 6

A test is like a Polaroid photo: it needs the right amount of time to develop. Look too soon and it is blank; wait too long and the picture looks wrong.

### Question 7

If a recipe calls for butter and you only have salt, you do not just use salt and call it butter. You get the right ingredient first.

### Question 8

Baking soda and vinegar only fizz correctly if you use the right amounts. Put in way too much of one and the reaction is ruined. The test needs the right amount.

### Question 9

Some food must stay in the fridge or it spoils. Reagents also have rules about where they must live so they keep working.

### Question 10

If milk sits out overnight, you would not just put it back and drink it. You would tell an adult and get fresh milk.

### Question 11

Old medicine past its date should not be taken, even if you feel sick and need it. Expired tests are the same: they get thrown out or set aside.

### Question 12

If the milk carton says it expired yesterday, you would not drink it even if it smells fine. You would pour it out and open a new one.

### Question 13

Some things only work right at the right temperature, like bread dough that will not rise in a cold kitchen. The test needs the right room temperature too.

### Question 14

A lot number is like the batch number on a batch of cookies, so if one batch has a problem you know exactly which cookies to check.

### Question 15

When you get a new batch of anything, you check it works before trusting it. A new lot of tests gets a checkup before it is used on real patients.

### Question 16

A control solution is like a practice question with a known answer. If the test gives the right known answer, you know it is working.

### Question 17

A class has one set of rules so everyone plays the same game. The office has one written procedure so every test is done the same right way.

### Question 18

If you forget the next move in a board game, you check the rule book instead of guessing. If you still do not know, you ask an adult.

### Question 19

A paper plate is used once and thrown away; you would not wash and share it. Single-use tests are the same.

### Question 20

If a cracker falls on the floor, you throw it away and get a new one instead of eating it. The test strip gets the same treatment.

### Question 21

Puzzle pieces from different boxes might look alike but do not fit the picture. Test strips and readers from different makers do not go together either.

### Question 22

If you have two boxes of different crayons, you keep them in their own boxes and label them so you know which crayon came from where.

### Question 23

Quality control is like checking your scale with a known weight before you weigh yourself, so you know the number is right.

### Question 24

Internal QC is like checking your own homework with an answer key. External QC is like turning your homework in to a teacher who checks it against everyone else.

### Question 25

Internal QC is like checking a calculator by typing a problem you already know the answer to.

### Question 26

External QC is like a spelling test from the teacher where your answers are compared to the correct ones and to the rest of the class.

### Question 27

A positive control checks the test says 'yes' when the answer is yes, and a negative control checks it says 'no' when the answer is no. You want both to work.

### Question 28

You test a new box of crayons by making sure each color actually colors before you use it on your big drawing. New tests get checked before real use.

### Question 29

The recipe and the house rules say when to check the oven temperature; you do not skip it just because you are busy.

### Question 30

You set an alarm to take medicine on time; you do not just take it when you remember. QC works the same way, on a schedule.

### Question 31

A QC log is like a scorecard you keep so you can prove you practiced and see how you did over time.

### Question 32

A complete QC note is like writing who, when, what, and which batch on a homework page so anyone can check it later.

### Question 33

If the smoke detector battery is dead, you do not pretend it is fine; you fix it before trusting it. A failed control means stop and fix first.

### Question 34

If both brake lights on a car are out, you do not drive anyway; you pull over and get help. Both controls failing means stop and get help.

### Question 35

If one of two traffic lights is broken, the intersection is still unsafe. One good control plus one bad control is still not safe.

### Question 36

Even on the busiest day, if the safety check fails you stop, because being busy does not make an unsafe thing safe.

### Question 37

You check a test score against the answer key, not against how you feel. The kit insert is the answer key for controls.

### Question 38

You fix the problem and re-check that it works, then write down what you fixed before starting again.

### Question 39

A report card must show your real grades, not made-up ones, or no one can trust it. QC logs must show the real results.

### Question 40

You cannot write down a score for a game you did not play. Writing a control result you did not run is making up a score.

### Question 41

Proficiency testing is like a surprise quiz: you answer honestly and on your own, because that is how the teacher finds out what you really know.

### Question 42

A fish tank needs its temperature checked on a schedule so the fish stay healthy. Reagent fridges get checked and written down on schedule too.

### Question 43

Writing the batch number on each cookie box lets you find every cookie from a bad batch. Lot numbers do the same for test results.

### Question 44

Two identical ovens can still heat differently, so you check each one. Each device gets its own check.

### Question 45

When you fix a bike, you write down what was broken and what you fixed so the next person understands. QC fixes get written down the same way.

### Question 46

Homework answers and practice answers go in different columns so they do not get mixed up. QC and patient results stay separate too.

### Question 47

You check your shoes are tied before a race, not after you trip. QC is the check before testing.

### Question 48

Once you open a jar of sauce, you write the date on it because it only lasts so long after opening. Reagents get a date written too.

### Question 49

If your alarm clock fails once and works the next day, you still find out why it failed instead of hoping it never fails again.

### Question 50

If one rule says check twice and another says check once, you check twice to be safe and ask which rule is right.

### Question 51

You write down the score right after the game, not hours later from memory. Results get written down right away.

### Question 52

Saying '5' without saying 5 inches or 5 miles means nothing. A result needs its units too.

### Question 53

A good entry is like signing and dating your artwork so everyone knows who made it and when. Test entries get signed and dated too.

### Question 54

If you write a phone number down right away, you get it right. If you wait, you might mix up the digits.

### Question 55

If your note is too messy to read, the teacher might read the wrong answer. Clear handwriting matters for results.

### Question 56

You cross out a mistake with one neat line and write the right answer next to it, then sign it, so everyone sees what changed.

### Question 57

You sign your own artwork, not someone else's. You record the test you did, not someone else's.

### Question 58

The assistant is like the messenger who delivers the test score to the teacher; the teacher decides what it means.

### Question 59

If a picture is blurry, you do not guess what it shows; you follow the instructions or ask for help. A faint line gets the same careful handling.

### Question 60

You write down the real score, not the score your friend wanted. Results are written exactly as they are.

### Question 61

Copying a number is like copying a phone number: you write it exactly, not a rounded version.

### Question 62

If you put your letter in the wrong mailbox, you fix it right away and tell an adult, not hide it.

### Question 63

Practice scores and real game scores go in different notebooks so no one confuses a practice score for the real thing.

### Question 64

If a thermometer goes past its highest number, you say 'it went past the top' instead of making up a number.

### Question 65

If a fire alarm rings, you tell the right person right away; you do not wait or turn it off.

### Question 66

An invalid result is like a broken ruler: you cannot trust its number, so you do not use it.

### Question 67

The control line is like a 'ready' light. If it never turns on, the machine did not start right, so you do not trust the answer.

### Question 68

A control line is like the green light that says the machine finished properly; without it, the answer does not count.

### Question 69

Expired milk cannot be used to test a recipe, and expired control solution cannot be used to test the test.

### Question 70

If the safety check fails, you stop and tell the person in charge before doing anything else.

### Question 71

If you measure with the wrong cup, you pour it out and measure again with the right cup; you do not keep the wrong amount.

### Question 72

Passing the practice test does not mean you can change the rules for the real test. You still follow the rules.

### Question 73

If every answer on a quiz suddenly looks wrong, you check the answer key, not the students. Recheck the test system.

### Question 74

If your car's gas gauge is creeping toward empty, you find a gas station before you run out, not after.

### Question 75

You ask an adult for help when something is broken, confusing, or surprising. That is escalation.

### Question 76

The assistant is the messenger, and the clinician is the one who reads the letter and explains it.

### Question 77

The assistant politely says the teacher will explain the grade; the assistant is not the one who decides what it means.

### Question 78

When something breaks, you write down what broke and what you did to fix it, so everyone knows.

### Question 79

If the wrapper on a snack is torn, you do not eat it. A torn test wrapper means do not use that test.

### Question 80

You put the spoiled milk on a separate shelf marked 'do not drink' so no one grabs it by mistake.

### Question 81

If you spill part of a quiz, you tell the teacher instead of pretending it did not happen.

### Question 82

A positive control is like making sure a fire alarm rings when there is real smoke. It ringing on cue is a good sign.

### Question 83

If a test for 'nothing there' says 'something is there,' something is wrong with the test, so you stop and get help.

### Question 84

If the fridge lost power, you would not feed the food to a guest to see if it is okay. You check it or throw it out.

### Question 85

The assistant is like a reliable teammate who follows the playbook, keeps score honestly, and tells the coach when something looks wrong.
